These inconsistencies may be typos or errors, and they weaken confidence in the NBC text's precision.
differences.quote: Cole Tomas Allen, the man arrested at the White House Correspondent's Dinner Association dinner

result.score_reason: Both outlets report the same charge with similar factual content and neither quotes officials, defense lawyers, or the suspect. The main differences are wording: the NY Post headline keeps "Alleged" but uses the punchier "hit with" and adds penalty stakes, while NBC drops the hedge and states "gunman" more flatly. Editorial line or audience may explain this, but the texts are too short to say, and neither article shows strong framing.
shared_facts: Cole Allen (spelled differently in each article) is the suspect in the White House Correspondents' Dinner shooting.
A new terrorism-related charge has been added to his case.
The charge is a federal case that the articles describe as new.
result.summary: Both outlets report that a federal terrorism-related charge was added against Cole Allen in the White House Correspondents' Dinner shooting, with small differences in hedging, emphasis on penalties, and procedural detail.
